commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Unify sync, async and dispatch execution (#24986)

`iree-benchmark-module` had separate synchronous, asynchronous, and
generated-dispatch execution paths that applied output processing,
replay capture, and profiling flushes inconsistently. Run them through
one batch lifecycle so discovery resolves each function's ABI and
iteration accounting once and every execution model shares the measured
loop.

The shared lifecycle fixes several inconsistencies:

- Retain asynchronous outputs for `--enable_output_processing`.
- Supply fence arguments for discovered asynchronous functions.
- Use the generated repeat count for dispatch benchmarks selected with
`--function`.
- Handle non-power-of-two `--batch_concurrency` without reading past the
invocation list.
- Return recording devices from context setup so asynchronous fences
participate in replay capture.

Errors go to stderr with `EXIT_FAILURE`, matching `iree-run-module`.
Output processing requires a single benchmarked function, and
nonpositive batch size or concurrency is rejected. Device profiling ends
before output processing.

Assisted by AI.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[iree-benchmark-module] Unify sync, async and dispatch execution (#24986)

replay capture, and profiling flushes inconsistently. Run them through
one batch lifecycle so discovery resolves each function's ABI and
iteration accounting once and every execution model shares the measured
loop.

The shared lifecycle fixes several inconsistencies:

- Retain asynchronous outputs for `--enable_output_processing`.
- Supply fence arguments for discovered asynchronous functions.
- Use the generated repeat count for dispatch benchmarks selected with
`--function`.
- Handle non-power-of-two `--batch_concurrency` without reading past the
invocation list.
- Return recording devices from context setup so asynchronous fences
participate in replay capture.

Errors go to stderr with `EXIT_FAILURE`, matching `iree-run-module`.
Output processing requires a single benchmarked function, and
nonpositive batch size or concurrency is rejected. Device profiling ends
before output processing.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions (#24966)

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves, and
add the function pass
`iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings` for propagation
outside dispatches. Hoisting keeps its existing behavior. The new pass
stops at existing dispatches and block boundaries, and constant CSE
stays disabled because Flow regions do not materialize constants
themselves.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings` runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps `set_encoding` with `tensor.cast`
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
They stay separate until bubbling through generic ops goes through the
encoding propagation interfaces (TODO(#20179)).
- Bubbling now stops at `set_encoding` ops whose encoding is not an
`EncodingAttr`, such as `#iree_encoding.padding`, instead of crashing.
`iree-dispatch-creation-hoist-encoding-ops` could already hit this
within dispatches; both passes have a regression test.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental
early data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions (#24966)

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves, and
add the function pass
`iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings` for propagation
outside dispatches. Hoisting keeps its existing behavior. The new pass
stops at existing dispatches and block boundaries, and constant CSE
stays disabled because Flow regions do not materialize constants
themselves.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings` runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps `set_encoding` with `tensor.cast`
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
They stay separate until bubbling through generic ops goes through the
encoding propagation interfaces (TODO(#20179)).
- Bubbling now stops at `set_encoding` ops whose encoding is not an
`EncodingAttr`, such as `#iree_encoding.padding`, instead of crashing.
`iree-dispatch-creation-hoist-encoding-ops` could already hit this
within dispatches; both passes have a regression test.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental
early data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Move the existing Linux Clang job to Ubuntu 24.04 with official Mesa RADV
packages and validation layers. Reuse its regular IREE build for HIP and
Vulkan e2e tests, with RADV compiling the existing SPIR-V modules for
gfx1100 and gfx1201.

Use one packaged TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261006 for both suites. This wheel
includes the rocjitsu SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run both simulator suites after a successful
build even if an earlier test suite fails.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

Assisted-by: codex

Move the existing Linux Clang job to Ubuntu 24.04 with official Mesa RADV
packages and validation layers. Reuse its regular IREE build for HIP and
Vulkan e2e tests, with RADV compiling the existing SPIR-V modules for
gfx1100 and gfx1201.

Use one packaged TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261006 for both suites. This wheel
includes the rocjitsu SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run both simulator suites after a successful
build even if an earlier test suite fails.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

Assisted-by: codex
name: Test AMD W7900 / test_w7900

[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Move the existing Linux Clang job to Ubuntu 24.04 with official Mesa RADV
packages. Reuse its regular IREE build for HIP and Vulkan e2e tests, with
RADV compiling the existing SPIR-V modules for gfx1100 and gfx1201.

Use one packaged TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261006 for both suites. This wheel
includes the rocjitsu SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run both simulator suites after a successful
build even if an earlier test suite fails.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

Assisted-by: codex
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings (#24980)

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its
generated dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers
are not exposed as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel
therefore need to maintain their own build definitions to package Python
bindings that match the compiler they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler
packages against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding
definitions alongside the sources they describe. The bindings use
`IREECompiler`'s shared C API so Python code can inspect and construct
IR, then invoke the compiler using the same MLIR implementation.
Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

Assisted-By: GPT-6-Astra

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Keep strided input maps when the producer can fuse (#24950)

Factoring `dim * cst` strides out of a contraction-like generic inserts
a strided `tensor.extract_slice` between the contraction and its input.
When the input has an elementwise producer (a dequantize feeding a 1x1
stride-2 convolution, say), the slice blocks both fusion paths:
elementwise fusion requires the producer to directly define the
consumer's operand, and tile-based producer fusion only supports
unit-stride slices. Codegen falls back to materializing the producer as
a whole-tensor stack allocation in every workgroup: a 3.2 MB alloca for
a 1x256x56x56xf32 dequantize, well over the 32 KB stack limit, and the
compile fails.

Skip the factoring only when the strided input's producer can fuse
elementwise into the contraction and into every other user of its
result, so the fusion actually eliminates the producer. Codegen then
merges the producer into the contraction, which reads the input directly
through the strided map with no intermediate tensor. Producers that are
materialized anyway (e.g. a result also returned from the function) keep
the factored projected-permutation input map.

Strided contractions with a fusable producer now lower through the
generic path instead of contraction selection such as AMDGPU MFMA, the
original motivation for the factoring, in exchange for eliminating the
intermediate tensor. Strided contractions on dispatch-boundary inputs
keep the factored form.

Fixes #24752

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Keep strided input maps when the producer can fuse (#24950)

Factoring `dim * cst` strides out of a contraction-like generic inserts
a strided `tensor.extract_slice` between the contraction and its input.
When the input has an elementwise producer (a dequantize feeding a 1x1
stride-2 convolution, say), the slice blocks both fusion paths:
elementwise fusion requires the producer to directly define the
consumer's operand, and tile-based producer fusion only supports
unit-stride slices. Codegen falls back to materializing the producer as
a whole-tensor stack allocation in every workgroup: a 3.2 MB alloca for
a 1x256x56x56xf32 dequantize, well over the 32 KB stack limit, and the
compile fails.

Skip the factoring only when the strided input's producer can fuse
elementwise into the contraction and into every other user of its
result, so the fusion actually eliminates the producer. Codegen then
merges the producer into the contraction, which reads the input directly
through the strided map with no intermediate tensor. Producers that are
materialized anyway (e.g. a result also returned from the function) keep
the factored projected-permutation input map.

Strided contractions with a fusable producer now lower through the
generic path instead of contraction selection such as AMDGPU MFMA, the
original motivation for the factoring, in exchange for eliminating the
intermediate tensor. Strided contractions on dispatch-boundary inputs
keep the factored form.

Fixes #24752

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 528d3dcb (#24908)

Updates torch-mlir from its July 7 upstream baseline to
[`llvm/torch-mlir@528d3dcb`](https://github.com/llvm/torch-mlir/commit/528d3dcb9a2288743b62df9f4937b1689787e38a),
using
[`iree-org/torch-mlir@137b8fb8`](https://github.com/iree-org/torch-mlir/commit/137b8fb8596f4c8091f69535e5153f35b7ece311)
(`sm-iree-integrates/torch-20261002`) adapted to IREE's current LLVM
revision.

On top of canonical torch-mlir, the integration branch carries the
adaptation patches already on IREE's current pin that upstream does not
have yet: the LLVM submodule bump, `SymbolOpInterface` for
`ClassTypeOp`/`GlobalSlotOp`, and the TMTensor strict-properties
assembly fix. The `DenseMapInfo` and `RegionSuccessor` adaptations from
the previous pin are now upstream and were dropped.

ONNX op test expectations:

- Now passing, removed from `expected_run_failures` in the CI-exercised
configs:
`averagepool_3d_dilations_large_count_include_pad_is_0_ceil_mode_is_True`,
`nonmaxsuppression_flipped_coordinates`, `reduce_{max,min}_bool_inputs`.


- `test_reversesequence_time` now fails to compile on llvm-cpu and is
marked as an expected compile failure. ReverseSequence now lowers to an
`scf.for` over the time axis, so each dispatch reverses a column picked
by a dynamic offset. The resulting `vector.gather` reads a strided
column subview with a dynamic offset, which neither
`RemoveStrideFromGatherSource` (bails on dynamic offsets) nor
`Gather1DToConditionalLoads` (rejects non-unit inner stride) handles, so
the gather reaches LLVM conversion unlowered. The proper fix is
dynamic-offset support in the upstream MLIR gather lowering.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Name the new pass after the ops it propagates through

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings was hard to tell
apart from iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings. Both run outside
dispatches; the difference is that the new pass moves encodings through
linalg.generic ops, while the existing one only swaps set_encoding ops
with tensor.cast producers. Rename it to
iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings-through-generic-ops and keep
its definition next to the existing pass.

Test that propagation does not cross the boundary of an existing
dispatch region in either direction, and describe the expectations in
terms of dispatch regions rather than early and late placement.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings was hard to tell
apart from iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings. Both run outside
dispatches; the difference is that the new pass moves encodings through
linalg.generic ops, while the existing one only swaps set_encoding ops
with tensor.cast producers. Rename it to
iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings-through-generic-ops and keep
its definition next to the existing pass.

Test that propagation does not cross the boundary of an existing
dispatch region in either direction, and describe the expectations in
terms of dispatch regions rather than early and late placement.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings was hard to tell
apart from iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings. Both run outside
dispatches; the difference is that the new pass moves encodings through
linalg.generic ops, while the existing one only swaps set_encoding ops
with tensor.cast producers. Rename it to
iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings-through-generic-ops and keep
its definition next to the existing pass.

Test that propagation does not cross the boundary of an existing
dispatch region in either direction, and describe the expectations in
terms of dispatch regions rather than early and late placement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: linux_arm64_clang

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Run HIP and Vulkan e2e tests in a dedicated Ubuntu 24.04 job using official
Mesa RADV packages. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules for gfx1100 and
gfx1201 and let RADV compile them to the simulated GPU's instructions.

Use one packaged TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261006 for both suites. This wheel
includes the rocjitsu SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run Vulkan even when HIP tests fail.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

Assisted-by: codex
name: pre-commit

[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Run HIP and Vulkan e2e tests in a dedicated Ubuntu 24.04 job using official
Mesa RADV packages. Reuse the existing SPIR-V modules for gfx1100 and
gfx1201 and let RADV compile them to the simulated GPU's instructions.

Use one packaged TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261006 for both suites. This wheel
includes the rocjitsu SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run Vulkan even when HIP tests fail.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

Assisted-by: codex

commit_message:
[Integrate] Update torch-mlir to 528d3dcb (#24908)

Updates torch-mlir from its July 7 upstream baseline to
[`llvm/torch-mlir@528d3dcb`](https://github.com/llvm/torch-mlir/commit/528d3dcb9a2288743b62df9f4937b1689787e38a),
using
[`iree-org/torch-mlir@137b8fb8`](https://github.com/iree-org/torch-mlir/commit/137b8fb8596f4c8091f69535e5153f35b7ece311)
(`sm-iree-integrates/torch-20261002`) adapted to IREE's current LLVM
revision.

On top of canonical torch-mlir, the integration branch carries the
adaptation patches already on IREE's current pin that upstream does not
have yet: the LLVM submodule bump, `SymbolOpInterface` for
`ClassTypeOp`/`GlobalSlotOp`, and the TMTensor strict-properties
assembly fix. The `DenseMapInfo` and `RegionSuccessor` adaptations from
the previous pin are now upstream and were dropped.

ONNX op test expectations:

- Now passing, removed from `expected_run_failures` in the CI-exercised
configs:
`averagepool_3d_dilations_large_count_include_pad_is_0_ceil_mode_is_True`,
`nonmaxsuppression_flipped_coordinates`, `reduce_{max,min}_bool_inputs`.


- `test_reversesequence_time` now fails to compile on llvm-cpu and is
marked as an expected compile failure. ReverseSequence now lowers to an
`scf.for` over the time axis, so each dispatch reverses a column picked
by a dynamic offset. The resulting `vector.gather` reads a strided
column subview with a dynamic offset, which neither
`RemoveStrideFromGatherSource` (bails on dynamic offsets) nor
`Gather1DToConditionalLoads` (rejects non-unit inner stride) handles, so
the gather reaches LLVM conversion unlowered. The proper fix is
dynamic-offset support in the upstream MLIR gather lowering.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Normalize contraction dimensions outside dispatches (#24965)

Contractions with several contiguous M, N, K or batch dimensions can
miss data-tiling encodings because dimension collapsing currently runs
inside dispatches.

Add a function pass that reuses the existing collapse rules outside
dispatches and restores the original tensor shapes at the op boundaries.
Leave existing dispatches (regions and workgroups) and ops with a preset
compilation info or lowering config alone, since those configurations
refer to the original loops.

No pipeline runs the pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental early
data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

Assisted by AI.
name: pkgci_summary / summary

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Unify sync, async and dispatch execution (#24986)

`iree-benchmark-module` had separate synchronous, asynchronous, and
generated-dispatch execution paths that applied output processing,
replay capture, and profiling flushes inconsistently. Run them through
one batch lifecycle so discovery resolves each function's ABI and
iteration accounting once and every execution model shares the measured
loop.

The shared lifecycle fixes several inconsistencies:

- Retain asynchronous outputs for `--enable_output_processing`.
- Supply fence arguments for discovered asynchronous functions.
- Use the generated repeat count for dispatch benchmarks selected with
`--function`.
- Handle non-power-of-two `--batch_concurrency` without reading past the
invocation list.
- Return recording devices from context setup so asynchronous fences
participate in replay capture.

Errors go to stderr with `EXIT_FAILURE`, matching `iree-run-module`.
Output processing requires a single benchmarked function, and
nonpositive batch size or concurrency is rejected. Device profiling ends
before output processing.

Assisted by AI.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: pkgci_summary / summary

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Add dispatch timing rows

Add --dispatch_statistics for a per-function breakdown of where a
benchmark spends its dispatch time. After each measured repetition,
Google Benchmark reruns the registered benchmark outside the measured
interval with a lightweight HAL statistics session on every device, so
profiling uses the same function ABI, batch accounting and asynchronous
concurrency as measurement. The rows appear under their benchmark in
console, JSON and CSV output, including --benchmark_out files, whose
formatter is selected from Google Benchmark's parsed flags. Conflicting
profiling, capture and replay flags are rejected before any session
starts or the replay file is opened.

To start sessions with explicit options, the tooling profiling session
type is now iree_hal_profiling_session_t with _begin, _flush and _end
functions, and iree_hal_profiling_from_flags_is_requested validates the
profiling flags without starting a session. The device profiling flags
of iree-benchmark-module now cover every device instead of the first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Unify sync, async and dispatch execution (#24986)

`iree-benchmark-module` had separate synchronous, asynchronous, and
generated-dispatch execution paths that applied output processing,
replay capture, and profiling flushes inconsistently. Run them through
one batch lifecycle so discovery resolves each function's ABI and
iteration accounting once and every execution model shares the measured
loop.

The shared lifecycle fixes several inconsistencies:

- Retain asynchronous outputs for `--enable_output_processing`.
- Supply fence arguments for discovered asynchronous functions.
- Use the generated repeat count for dispatch benchmarks selected with
`--function`.
- Handle non-power-of-two `--batch_concurrency` without reading past the
invocation list.
- Return recording devices from context setup so asynchronous fences
participate in replay capture.

Errors go to stderr with `EXIT_FAILURE`, matching `iree-run-module`.
Output processing requires a single benchmarked function, and
nonpositive batch size or concurrency is rejected. Device profiling ends
before output processing.

Assisted by AI.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Name the new pass after the ops it propagates through

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings was hard to tell
apart from iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings. Both run outside
dispatches; the difference is that the new pass moves encodings through
linalg.generic ops, while the existing one only swaps set_encoding ops
with tensor.cast producers. Rename it to
iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings-through-generic-ops and keep
its definition next to the existing pass.

Test that propagation does not cross the boundary of an existing
dispatch region in either direction, and describe the expectations in
terms of dispatch regions rather than early and late placement.

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Keep strided input maps when the producer can fuse (#24950)

Factoring `dim * cst` strides out of a contraction-like generic inserts
a strided `tensor.extract_slice` between the contraction and its input.
When the input has an elementwise producer (a dequantize feeding a 1x1
stride-2 convolution, say), the slice blocks both fusion paths:
elementwise fusion requires the producer to directly define the
consumer's operand, and tile-based producer fusion only supports
unit-stride slices. Codegen falls back to materializing the producer as
a whole-tensor stack allocation in every workgroup: a 3.2 MB alloca for
a 1x256x56x56xf32 dequantize, well over the 32 KB stack limit, and the
compile fails.

Skip the factoring only when the strided input's producer can fuse
elementwise into the contraction and into every other user of its
result, so the fusion actually eliminates the producer. Codegen then
merges the producer into the contraction, which reads the input directly
through the strided map with no intermediate tensor. Producers that are
materialized anyway (e.g. a result also returned from the function) keep
the factored projected-permutation input map.

Strided contractions with a fusable producer now lower through the
generic path instead of contraction selection such as AMDGPU MFMA, the
original motivation for the factoring, in exchange for eliminating the
intermediate tensor. Strided contractions on dispatch-boundary inputs
keep the factored form.

Fixes #24752

consumer's operand, and tile-based producer fusion only supports
unit-stride slices. Codegen falls back to materializing the producer as
a whole-tensor stack allocation in every workgroup: a 3.2 MB alloca for
a 1x256x56x56xf32 dequantize, well over the 32 KB stack limit, and the
compile fails.

Skip the factoring only when the strided input's producer can fuse
elementwise into the contraction and into every other user of its
result, so the fusion actually eliminates the producer. Codegen then
merges the producer into the contraction, which reads the input directly
through the strided map with no intermediate tensor. Producers that are
materialized anyway (e.g. a result also returned from the function) keep
the factored projected-permutation input map.

Strided contractions with a fusable producer now lower through the
generic path instead of contraction selection such as AMDGPU MFMA, the
original motivation for the factoring, in exchange for eliminating the
intermediate tensor. Strided contractions on dispatch-boundary inputs
keep the factored form.

Fixes #24752

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings (#24980)

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its
generated dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers
are not exposed as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel
therefore need to maintain their own build definitions to package Python
bindings that match the compiler they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler
packages against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding
definitions alongside the sources they describe. The bindings use
`IREECompiler`'s shared C API so Python code can inspect and construct
IR, then invoke the compiler using the same MLIR implementation.
Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

commit_message:
[CI] Add RDNA3 and RDNA4 Vulkan e2e tests under rocjitsu

Move the existing Linux Clang job to Ubuntu 24.04 with official Mesa RADV
packages and validation layers. Reuse its regular IREE build for HIP and
Vulkan e2e tests, with RADV compiling the existing SPIR-V modules for
gfx1100 and gfx1201.

Use one packaged TheRock SDK 10.2.0a20261006 for both suites. This wheel
includes the rocjitsu SDMA count fix from
https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-systems/pull/12708.

Verify the RADV driver and simulated PCI device identity before CTest.
Use eight test workers, a 60-minute Vulkan step timeout, and per-target
logs and JUnit results. Run both simulator suites after a successful
build even if an earlier test suite fails.

Order PluginABIHash.h generation before consumers in child directories
compile, fixing a missing dependency exposed by the fresh build.

Assisted-by: codex
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_models :: amdgpu_hip_rdna3

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions (#24966)

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves, and
add the function pass
`iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-data-tiling-encodings` for propagation
outside dispatches. Hoisting keeps its existing behavior. The new pass
stops at existing dispatches and block boundaries, and constant CSE
stays disabled because Flow regions do not materialize constants
themselves.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings` runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps `set_encoding` with `tensor.cast`
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
They stay separate until bubbling through generic ops goes through the
encoding propagation interfaces (TODO(#20179)).
- Bubbling now stops at `set_encoding` ops whose encoding is not an
`EncodingAttr`, such as `#iree_encoding.padding`, instead of crashing.
`iree-dispatch-creation-hoist-encoding-ops` could already hit this
within dispatches; both passes have a regression test.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental
early data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.
